Gloucester Township Municipal Court: Location, Hours, Contact Info, and Services

The Gloucester Township Municipal Court is a key judicial body in Camden County, New Jersey, handling a wide range of cases, including traffic violations, criminal offenses, and housing code violations. Below is a comprehensive guide to the court’s location, hours, contact information, and services to help you navigate its processes effectively.

Gloucester Township Municipal Court Location and Contact Information

  • Address: 1261 Chews Landing Rd, Clementon, NJ 08021, United States
  • Google Maps: Gloucester Township Municipal Court Location
  • Phone: 856-228-4000
  • Website: Gloucester Township Municipal Court Official Website
  • Email: patricia.carroll@njcourts.gov

Court Hours

  • Monday to Thursday: 8:00 AM – 5:45 PM
  • Friday to Sunday: Closed

Key Personnel

  • Judge: Nicholas Trabosh
  • Court Administrator: Patty Carroll
  • Chief Prosecutor: Chris Long, Esq., Dan Long, Esq.
  • Clerk of Courts: Nancy Power

Jurisdiction and Case Types

The Gloucester Township Municipal Court handles:

  • Traffic and vehicle violations (speeding, parking tickets, etc.)
  • Criminal offenses (disorderly conduct, theft, simple assault)
  • Housing and construction code violations
  • Felony cases (e.g., drug possession, shoplifting)

How to Access Court Records

Court records for Gloucester Township Municipal Court can be accessed through:

  1. Online Search: Use the case number, name, city/state, or address.
  2. In-Person Visit: Visit the town or county clerk’s office.
  3. Mail Request: Submit a record request form with the required fees.

Note: Some records, such as confidential criminal cases, may only be available in person at the county clerk’s office.

Payment Options for Fines and Tickets

Pay your fines or tickets through:

  1. In-Person: Visit the court during working hours. Accepts cash, checks, or cards (2.99% processing fee for credit cards).
  2. Online: Use the New Jersey Online Payment Portal.
  3. Mail: Send a certified check or money order to:
    Violation Bureau, Blackwood, NJ 08012, United States
    Note: Include your citation number and a self-addressed stamped envelope for a receipt.

Felony Cases Handled

The court handles felony cases such as:

  • Drug possession (marijuana under 50 grams)
  • Theft and shoplifting
  • Simple assault
  • Trespassing

These cases are remanded to the Superior Court of Camden County after initial processing.

Municipal Assessor’s Office Responsibilities

The Municipal Assessor’s Office maintains property records for over 22,500 parcels in Gloucester Township. Responsibilities include:

  • Updating property records (names, addresses, maps)
  • Reviewing property tax deductions

How to Submit a Plea by Mail

If you’ve received a traffic or parking ticket, you can submit a plea by mail:

  1. Download the Plea Form from the court’s website.
  2. Choose between:
    • Guilty Plea: Admits violation; court will respond with fines or a court date.
    • Not Guilty Plea: Denies violation; court will schedule a trial date.
  3. Mail the completed form before the citation date.

When to Hire an Attorney

Hiring an attorney is recommended for:

  • Personal injury or accident cases
  • Driving under the influence (DUI) charges
  • Significant property damage cases
  • Pleading not guilty

An experienced attorney can help navigate the legal system and achieve a favorable outcome.

Consequences of Missing a Court Date

Failing to appear in court can result in:

  • Additional fines
  • Suspension of your driver’s license
  • Issuance of an arrest warrant

Contact the court immediately if you cannot attend your scheduled date.

Court Procedures

  1. Summons: If charged, you’ll receive a court date and time.
  2. Hearing: Present your case; the judge will make a decision based on evidence.
  3. Outcomes: Possible results include fines, community service, probation, or jail time.

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

  1. What is the dress code for court hearings?
    Proper attire is required. Avoid sleeveless, tight, or torn clothing.
  2. How do I contact the Clerk of Courts?
    Call 856-734-3534 during business hours.
  3. Can I appeal a court decision?
    Yes, consult an appellate attorney to explore your options.
  4. What happens if I have an arrest warrant?
    Contact a criminal defense attorney immediately to resolve the warrant.

Conclusion

The Gloucester Township Municipal Court plays a vital role in maintaining justice and order in Camden County. Whether you’re dealing with a traffic ticket, criminal charge, or housing violation, understanding the court’s procedures and services can help you navigate the legal system effectively. For further assistance, contact the court directly or consult with a qualified attorney.
